hypotheses: Large-copy singletonization and medium-panel component splitting remove different kinds of family context. Their contributions to recall gains and precision/functional regressions should be measured separately before changing either rule.

Deferring only large-copy singletonization may retain useful broad-panel context while preserving the medium-panel component safeguard; the opposite ablation tests whether medium-panel deferral is responsible for the observed losses or gains.

limitations: All current references are development-exposed; these two hypotheses are not independent confirmation.

Branch eligibility depends on protein-family and panel properties, not benchmark names. This is still a size-regime-specific mechanism whose transfer must be tested where the relevant branch actually activates.
Narrow fungal panels, including CGOB, cannot independently confirm the broad-panel large-copy branch; full CGOB also has known sequence overlap.
